title.purpose: Card headings, dialog titles, sidebar labels.

shadows.name: modal-scrim

motion.name: ease-out-standard

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions: button hover, link colour change, border shift.

motion.name: duration-enter

narrative.overview:
AniTrack is the visual equivalent of a meticulously kept shelf of physical media — each anime logged is a title that belongs to someone, a record of real time spent and genuine feeling. The UI is dark by design and by identity, not by fashion. It recedes so the content — cover art, titles, ratings — can be the loudest thing on screen.

The system rejects three failure modes by name: MyAnimeList's cluttered database aesthetic, generic SaaS templates (cream backgrounds, rounded ghost-card grids, hero-metric dashboards), and the chaotic otaku-site (competing colour families, banner overload, visual noise). What remains is something quieter and more deliberate — a space for obsessives who want their watch history to look as considered as it feels.

Density is controlled. Colour is restrained to a single violet/indigo axis. Typography leans on weight contrast, not size contrast. Motion is purposeful — a direct response to action, never decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Deep void background (#0f0f17) with tonal surface lifts, no shadows at rest
One primary accent (Violet Pulse #7c3aed) and one supporting accent (Indigo Spark #6366f1)
Weight-driven hierarchy: 900 display → 700 headline → 500 label → 400 body
Taut, precise components: 8px radius, clear border edges, no ghost-card pairing
Flat tonal elevation; depth from surface colour steps, not box-shadows

rules.name: The One Axis Rule
rules.body: The violet-to-indigo accent axis is the only expressive colour in the system. No greens for success, no blues for info, no additional brand hues.

rules.name: The Rarity Principle
rules.body: Violet Pulse appears on ≤15% of any given screen surface. If a page feels purple, the accent is being overused.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is expressed through font-weight before font-size. Reserve size increases for genuine level jumps (title → headline → display).

rules.name: The 14px Floor Rule
rules.body: No body text below 14px. The 10px format strip on AnimeCard is the sole permitted exception.

rules.name: The Tonal Stack Rule
rules.body: New surfaces must use one of three existing surface tokens: The Void / Obsidian / Deep Indigo. Do not introduce ad-hoc rgba() intermediate tones.

rules.name: The Shadow Exception Rule
rules.body: Box-shadows are reserved for two cases only: hover state on interactive cards (violet glow) and modal backdrop scrim. A shadow at rest is decoration masquerading as architecture.

dos: Let cover art carry the visual energy — keep surrounding chrome quiet
Use font-weight contrast (700 vs 400) before font-size contrast to establish hierarchy
Keep the accent to Violet Pulse (#7c3aed) and Indigo Spark (#6366f1) only
Show skeleton loading states for async content > 300ms using Deep Indigo blocks
Verify WCAG AA (4.5:1) whenever Slate Muted text appears on a non-standard surface
Give every interactive element a visible focus ring: 2px Violet Pulse, 2px ring-offset at The Void
Apply text-wrap: balance to all h1–h3 elements
Spatially separate destructive actions from primary actions
donts: Don't build anything that resembles MyAnimeList — no data-table sprawl or legacy tracker layout
Don't use warm-tinted or cream backgrounds, ghost-card grids with drop shadows, or numbered section markers
Don't introduce competing colour families or visual noise that competes with anime cover art
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient)
Don't use border-left > 1px as a coloured accent stripe on cards or alerts
Don't pair a 1px border AND a box-shadow > 8px blur on the same element at rest
Don't exceed 16px border-radius on cards or panels
Don't rely on colour alone to convey score quality — pair with star icon and numeric value
Don't put primary navigation behind a dropdown on desktop when authenticated
Don't add a fourth surface token — simplify the layout instead
